source_text: Sed deus sicut aeternus et rationalis, ita, opinor, et perfectus in omnibus: eritis enim perfecti quemadmodum pater uester, qui in caelis est. exhibe perfectam quoque bonitatem eius, etsi de imperfecta satis constat, quae neque naturalis inuenitur neque rationalis. nunc et alio ordine traducetur: nec iam imperfecta, immo et defecta, exigua et exhausta, quae, minor numero materiarum suarum, non in omnibus exhibetur. non enim omnes salui fiunt, sed pauciores omnibus et Iudaeis et Christianis creatoris. pluribus uero pereuntibus quomodo perfecta defenditur bonitas ex maiore parte cessatrix, paucis aliqua, pluribus nulla, cedens perditioni, partiaria exitii? quodsi plures salui non erunt, erit iam non bonitas, sed malitia perfectior. sicut enim bonitatis operatio est, quae facit saluos, ita malignitatis, quae non facit saluos. magis autem non faciens saluos, dum paucos facit, perfectior erit in non iuuando quam (in) iuuan lo. non poteris et in creatorem referre bonitatis in omnes defectionem. quem enim iudicem tenes, dispensatorem, si forte, bonitatis ostendis intellegendum, non profusorem, quod tuo deo uindicas. usque adeo hac sola eum praefers bonitate creatori. quam si solam profitetur et totam, nulli deesse debuerat. sed nolo iam de parte maiore pereuntium imperfectae bonitatis arguere deum Marcionis: sufficit ipsos, quos saluos facit, imperfectae salutis inuentos imperfectam bonitatem eius ostendere, scilicet anima tenus saluos, carne deperditos, quae apud illum non resurgit. unde haec dimidiatio salutis nisi ex defectione bonitatis? quid erat perfectae bonitatis quam totum hominem redigere in salutem, totum damnatum a creatore, totum a deo optimo adlectum? quod sciam, et caro tingitur apud illum, et caro de nuptiis tollitur, et caro in confessione nominis desaeuitur. sed et si carni delicta reputantur, praecedit animae reatus et culpae principatus animae potius adscribendus. cui caro ministri nomine occurrit. carens denique anima caro hactenus peccat. ita et in hoc iniusta bonitas et sic quoque imperfecta, innocentiorem substantiam relinquens in exitium, obsequio, non arbitrio delinquentem. cuius Christus etsi non induit ueritatem. ut tuae haeresi uisum est, imaginem tamen eius subire dignatus est. ipsum quod mentitus est illam, aliquid ei t debuit debuisse quid est autem homo aliud quam caro, siquidem nomen hominis materia corporalis, non animalis, ab auctore sortita est? et fecit hominem deus, inquit, limum de terra, non animam; anima enim de afflatu: et factus est homo in animam uiuam; quis? utique qui de limo: et posuit deus hominem in paradiso; quod finxit, non quod flauit: qui caro nunc, non qui anima. itaque si ita est. quo ore contendes perfectum bonitatis titulum, quae non iam a partitione speciali hominis liberandi defecit, sed a proprietate generali? si plena est gratia et solida misericordia, quae soli animae salutaris est, plus praestat haec uita, qua toti et integri fruimur. ceterum ex parte resurgere multari erit, non liberari.
pass_a_gloss: Perfect God must show perfect goodness; Marcion’s saves few and only to the soul; halved salvation = failed goodness; whole man must be saved; rising in part is punishment not liberation.
pass_b_english: But God, as he is eternal and rational, is also, I think, perfect in all things: for you will be perfect as your Father who is in the heavens. Show his perfect goodness too, even though there is enough certainty about an imperfect goodness that is found neither natural nor rational. Now it will also be led over in another order: no longer imperfect, but defective, scanty and exhausted — which, lesser in the number of its matters, is not shown in all. For not all are made safe, but fewer than all — both the Creator’s Jews and Christians. But with more perishing, how is goodness defended as perfect when it is idle in the greater part, some for a few, none for many, yielding to perdition, sharing out ruin? But if more will not be saved, it will already be not goodness but a more perfect malice. For as the working of goodness is what makes people safe, so of malignity what does not make them safe. But more by not making safe, while it makes few, it will be more perfect in not helping than in helping. You will not be able to refer to the Creator the failure of goodness toward all. For the one you hold as judge you show must be understood as a dispenser of goodness, if at all — not a pourer-out, which you claim for your god. So far do you prefer him to the Creator by this goodness alone. Which, if he professes it alone and whole, ought to have been lacking to no one. But I no longer want to argue Marcion’s god from the greater part of those who perish for imperfect goodness: it is enough that those he does make safe, found of imperfect salvation, show his imperfect goodness — safe as far as the soul, destroyed in the flesh, which with him does not rise. Where does this halving of salvation come from if not from a failure of goodness? What belonged to perfect goodness but to bring the whole man back into salvation — the whole condemned by the Creator, the whole chosen by the best God? As far as I know, with him flesh is also dipped, and flesh is taken from marriages, and flesh is savaged in confessing the name. But even if sins are charged to flesh, the soul’s guilt comes first and the headship of fault must be ascribed rather to the soul, to which flesh comes under the name of servant. Flesh lacking a soul, then, sins only so far. So in this too goodness is unjust and thus also imperfect, leaving the more innocent substance to ruin — offending by obedience, not by decision. And even if Christ did not put on its truth, as your heresy has it, he still deigned to undergo its image. The very fact that he lied about it owed it something. But what is man other than flesh, if the name of man was allotted by the author to bodily, not soul, matter? And God made man, it says, clay from the earth — not soul; for soul is from the breath: and man became a living soul; who? Surely the one from clay: and God placed man in paradise — what he formed, not what he blew; who is now flesh, not who is soul. So if it is so, with what mouth will you claim the title of perfect goodness, which has failed not only from a special partition of the man to be freed, but from the general property? If grace is full and mercy solid that is saving for the soul alone, this life which we enjoy whole and entire offers more. Whereas to rise in part will be to be punished, not freed.

lemmas.sense: for not all are made safe
safe as far as the soul, destroyed in the flesh
bring the whole man back into salvation

lemmas.lat: ex parte resurgere multari erit, non liberari
lemmas.sense: to rise in part will be to be punished, not freed

choices.why: salui fiunt / salus kept as ‘made safe/salvation’ to preserve forensic edge without altar-call tone.
dimidiatio salutis is Tertullian’s own cut — half a man saved.

choices.choose: rise in part… punished, not freed
choices.why: ex parte resurgere is eschatological body denial, not moral progress.

notes: Creator vs Marcion’s ‘best’ god; whole-man salvation vs soul-only.
